title: L'automne arrive!
oneGoal: Students will recognize autumn vocabulary through seasonal objects, visual supports, and nature exploration
decisionPoints: What autumn signs do students notice outside today?
Should we bring in real leaves or use pictures first?
Are students ready for outdoor exploration or classroom observation?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes seasonal awareness and introduces core autumn vocabulary through sensory experiences
realWorldConnection: How people notice and talk about changing seasons in their daily lives

title: Les feuilles dansent
oneGoal: Students will understand leaf-related vocabulary through movement, colors, and creative expression
decisionPoints: How do students naturally want to move like falling leaves?
Should we collect real leaves or create paper ones?
Are students ready for color-sorting activities with leaves?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by deepening leaf vocabulary while adding movement and color concepts
realWorldConnection: Observing how leaves change and fall in our neighborhood and parks

title: Les arbres en automne
oneGoal: Students will recognize tree vocabulary through observation, drawing, and simple descriptions
decisionPoints: Which trees can students see from our classroom window?
Should we focus on tree shapes or leaf changes first?
Are students ready for simple tree comparison activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by expanding from individual leaves to whole trees while reinforcing colors and movement
realWorldConnection: How trees provide homes for animals and beauty in our communities

title: Il fait frais!
oneGoal: Students will understand autumn weather vocabulary through clothing, sensory experiences, and weather observation
decisionPoints: What weather changes have students noticed recently?
Should we go outside to feel the weather or observe from windows?
Are students ready for weather prediction activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by connecting trees and leaves to weather changes while introducing sensory vocabulary
realWorldConnection: How autumn weather affects our clothing choices and daily activities

title: Les animaux se préparent
oneGoal: Students will learn about autumn animal behaviors through stories, movements, and visual supports
decisionPoints: Which animals do students know prepare for winter?
Should we use puppet stories or movement activities?
Are students ready for simple animal behavior discussions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by introducing animals while connecting to weather and seasonal changes
realWorldConnection: Observing how animals in our area get ready for colder weather

title: Première histoire d'automne
oneGoal: Students will listen to and respond to their first simple autumn story through pictures and gestures
decisionPoints: How long can students focus on story listening today?
Should we use props, pictures, or simple book illustrations?
Are students ready for story prediction activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by introducing storytelling while incorporating all previous autumn vocabulary
realWorldConnection: How families and communities share stories about seasons and nature

title: Les personnages d'automne
oneGoal: Students will identify story characters through dramatic play, props, and visual character cards
decisionPoints: Which characters most interest students?
Should we use costumes, masks, or simple props?
Are students ready for character role-playing activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by deepening story comprehension while introducing character vocabulary and dramatic play
realWorldConnection: How stories help us understand different personalities and feelings

title: Que se passe-t-il?
oneGoal: Students will understand story events through sequencing, retelling, and simple cause-and-effect activities
decisionPoints: How do students naturally sequence story events?
Should we use picture cards or act out the sequence?
Are students ready for 'what happens next' predictions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by adding sequence vocabulary while practicing character identification and story comprehension
realWorldConnection: Understanding how events connect in our daily lives and experiences

title: Mes mots d'automne
oneGoal: Students will practice autumn vocabulary through word games, picture matching, and creative expression
decisionPoints: Which vocabulary words are students most confident with?
Should we use movement games or quiet activities?
Are students ready for vocabulary choice-making games?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by consolidating vocabulary while introducing meta-language concepts about words and communication
realWorldConnection: How learning new words helps us express our thoughts and feelings

title: Raconter ensemble
oneGoal: Students will participate in collaborative storytelling through turns, prompts, and shared creative expression
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with taking turns speaking?
Should we use story starters or student-generated ideas?
Are students ready for partner or small group storytelling?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by encouraging oral expression while practicing vocabulary and story structure concepts
realWorldConnection: How families and friends create stories together during conversations and activities

title: Les sons d'automne
oneGoal: Students will explore autumn sounds through listening activities, sound-making, and vocabulary reinforcement
decisionPoints: What autumn sounds can students identify around us?
Should we go outside for sound exploration or create sounds in class?
Are students ready for sound-matching or sound-story activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by adding auditory elements to storytelling while reinforcing autumn vocabulary and oral expression
realWorldConnection: How different seasons bring different sounds to our environment

title: Notre histoire de classe
oneGoal: Students will begin creating a class autumn story through collaboration, illustration, and vocabulary application
decisionPoints: What story theme most interests the class?
Should we focus on illustrations or text first?
Are students ready for individual contributions to group story?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by synthesizing all previous learning into creative production while practicing collaborative skills
realWorldConnection: How communities work together to create and share meaningful stories

title: Révision et célébration
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate autumn vocabulary understanding through review activities, games, and assessment opportunities
decisionPoints: Which vocabulary needs more practice before assessment?
Should review be through games, stories, or individual activities?
Are students ready for self-assessment opportunities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by reviewing and consolidating all core learning while preparing for final demonstration
realWorldConnection: How reflecting on our learning helps us grow and feel proud of our progress

title: Présentation du livre
oneGoal: Students will present their class autumn book through sharing, reading aloud, and celebrating collaborative achievement
decisionPoints: How can each student contribute to the book presentation?
Should we invite other classes or keep presentation within our group?
Are students ready for individual speaking or prefer group participation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by culminating core curriculum through authentic presentation and celebration of learning
realWorldConnection: How sharing our creations builds confidence and connects us with others

title: Contes traditionnels d'automne
oneGoal: Students will explore traditional autumn stories from French culture through listening, discussion, and cultural connection (extension)
decisionPoints: Which traditional stories resonate most with students?
Should we focus on story enjoyment or cultural discussion?
Are students ready for comparing different story versions?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - deepens cultural understanding while practicing story comprehension skills
realWorldConnection: How different cultures have special stories about autumn and harvest time

title: Théâtre d'automne
oneGoal: Students will perform simple autumn scenes through dramatic play, costumes, and creative expression (extension)
decisionPoints: What type of performance best suits student comfort levels?
Should we use scripts or improvised dramatic play?
Are students ready for audience performance or classroom sharing?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - applies story knowledge through kinesthetic and dramatic expression
realWorldConnection: How acting and drama help us understand different perspectives and express creativity

title: Poésie d'automne
oneGoal: Students will explore autumn poetry through rhythm, rhyme, and creative language play (extension)
decisionPoints: How do students respond to different poetry rhythms?
Should we focus on listening to poetry or creating simple verses?
Are students ready for rhyming games and word play?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - introduces poetic language while reinforcing autumn vocabulary and oral expression
realWorldConnection: How poetry helps us express feelings about nature and seasonal changes

title: Légendes d'automne
oneGoal: Students will discover autumn legends and myths through storytelling, imagination, and cultural exploration (extension)
decisionPoints: Which legends capture student imagination most?
Should we create our own legends or explore existing ones?
Are students ready for discussing real versus imaginary elements?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - expands story genres while practicing vocabulary and comprehension skills
realWorldConnection: How legends help communities explain natural phenomena and preserve cultural wisdom

title: Automne autour du monde
oneGoal: Students will explore how autumn is celebrated in different French-speaking regions through photos, stories, and cultural comparison (extension)
decisionPoints: Which global autumn celebrations most interest students?
Should we use photos, videos, or guest speakers?
Are students ready for cultural comparison discussions?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - broadens cultural perspective while applying autumn vocabulary in global contexts
realWorldConnection: How people around the world experience and celebrate autumn in diverse ways

title: Notre festival d'automne
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their autumn learning journey through a festival combining stories, activities, and community sharing (extension)
decisionPoints: How can the festival honor each student's learning journey?
Should we include families or keep celebration classroom-focused?
What activities best showcase student growth and confidence?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - culminates the entire unit with comprehensive celebration and community building
realWorldConnection: How festivals and celebrations strengthen community bonds and honor seasonal transitions
